title: Ezekiel 16: The Harlot Redeemed by an Everlasting Covenant
body:
Read the chapter → [Ezekiel 16](/bible/ezekiel/16)

**[Ezekiel 16:1-7](/bible/ezekiel/16#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/ezekiel/16#v1)</sup> Again the word of the Lord came unto me, saying,
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/ezekiel/16#v2)</sup> Son of man, cause Jerusalem to know her abominations,
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/ezekiel/16#v3)</sup> And say, Thus saith the Lord God unto Jerusalem; Thy birth and thy nativity is of the land of Canaan; thy father was an Amorite, and thy mother an Hittite.
>
> <sup>[4](/bible/ezekiel/16#v4)</sup> And as for thy nativity, in the day thou wast born thy navel was not cut, neither wast thou washed in water to supple thee; thou wast not salted at all, nor swaddled at all.
>
> <sup>[5](/bible/ezekiel/16#v5)</sup> None eye pitied thee, to do any of these unto thee, to have compassion upon thee; but thou wast cast out in the open field, to the lothing of thy person, in the day that thou wast born.
>
> <sup>[6](/bible/ezekiel/16#v6)</sup> And when I passed by thee, and saw thee polluted in thine own blood, I said unto thee when thou wast in thy blood, Live; yea, I said unto thee when thou wast in thy blood, Live.
>
> <sup>[7](/bible/ezekiel/16#v7)</sup> I have caused thee to multiply as the bud of the field, and thou hast increased and waxen great, and thou art come to excellent ornaments: thy breasts are fashioned, and thine hair is grown, whereas thou wast naked and bare.

- The word of the Most High came to Ezekiel to cause Jerusalem to know her abominations: her birth and nativity is of the land of Canaan, her father an Amorite and her mother a Hittite.
- This is describing how we were acting as heathens, to make it plain.
- In the day she was born her navel was not cut, she was not washed, not salted, not swaddled; no eye pitied her, and she was cast out in the open field to the loathing of her person.
- When the Most High passed by and saw her polluted in her own blood, He said unto her, Live; He caused her to multiply as the bud of the field, and she increased and came to excellent ornaments.

**[Ezekiel 16:8-14](/bible/ezekiel/16#v8)**

> <sup>[8](/bible/ezekiel/16#v8)</sup> Now when I passed by thee, and looked upon thee, behold, thy time was the time of love; and I spread my skirt over thee, and covered thy nakedness: yea, I sware unto thee, and entered into a covenant with thee, saith the Lord God, and thou becamest mine.
>
> <sup>[9](/bible/ezekiel/16#v9)</sup> Then washed I thee with water; yea, I throughly washed away thy blood from thee, and I anointed thee with oil.
>
> <sup>[10](/bible/ezekiel/16#v10)</sup> I clothed thee also with broidered work, and shod thee with badgers’ skin, and I girded thee about with fine linen, and I covered thee with silk.
>
> <sup>[11](/bible/ezekiel/16#v11)</sup> I decked thee also with ornaments, and I put bracelets upon thy hands, and a chain on thy neck.
>
> <sup>[12](/bible/ezekiel/16#v12)</sup> And I put a jewel on thy forehead, and earrings in thine ears, and a beautiful crown upon thine head.
>
> <sup>[13](/bible/ezekiel/16#v13)</sup> Thus wast thou decked with gold and silver; and thy raiment was of fine linen, and silk, and broidered work; thou didst eat fine flour, and honey, and oil: and thou wast exceeding beautiful, and thou didst prosper into a kingdom.
>
> <sup>[14](/bible/ezekiel/16#v14)</sup> And thy renown went forth among the heathen for thy beauty: for it was perfect through my comeliness, which I had put upon thee, saith the Lord God.

- When the Most High passed by and looked upon her, her time was the time of love; He spread His skirt over her, covered her nakedness, sware unto her, and entered into a covenant with her, and she became His.
- He washed her with water, anointed her with oil, clothed her with broidered work and fine linen, decked her with ornaments, bracelets, a chain, a jewel, earrings, and a beautiful crown of gold and silver.
- She was exceeding beautiful and prospered into a kingdom, and her renown went forth among the heathen for her beauty, for it was perfect through the comeliness the Most High had put upon her.
- This is how the Most High took us, built us up into a mighty nation, and beautified us.

**[Ezekiel 16:15-19](/bible/ezekiel/16#v15)**

> <sup>[15](/bible/ezekiel/16#v15)</sup> But thou didst trust in thine own beauty, and playedst the harlot because of thy renown, and pouredst out thy fornications on every one that passed by; his it was.
>
> <sup>[16](/bible/ezekiel/16#v16)</sup> And of thy garments thou didst take, and deckedst thy high places with divers colours, and playedst the harlot thereupon: the like things shall not come, neither shall it be so.
>
> <sup>[17](/bible/ezekiel/16#v17)</sup> Thou hast also taken thy fair jewels of my gold and of my silver, which I had given thee, and madest to thyself images of men, and didst commit whoredom with them,
>
> <sup>[18](/bible/ezekiel/16#v18)</sup> And tookest thy broidered garments, and coveredst them: and thou hast set mine oil and mine incense before them.
>
> <sup>[19](/bible/ezekiel/16#v19)</sup> My meat also which I gave thee, fine flour, and oil, and honey, wherewith I fed thee, thou hast even set it before them for a sweet savour: and thus it was, saith the Lord God.

- But she trusted in her own beauty and played the harlot because of her renown, and poured out her fornications on everyone that passed by.
- We got haughty, we trusted in our own beauty, and we began to play the harlot; the scriptures then explain what that means.
- She took her garments and made high places decked with divers colors, took the fair jewels of the Most High's gold and silver and made herself images of men, and set His oil, meat, fine flour, and honey before them for a sweet savour.

**[Ezekiel 16:20-22](/bible/ezekiel/16#v20)**

> <sup>[20](/bible/ezekiel/16#v20)</sup> Moreover thou hast taken thy sons and thy daughters, whom thou hast borne unto me, and these hast thou sacrificed unto them to be devoured. Is this of thy whoredoms a small matter,
>
> <sup>[21](/bible/ezekiel/16#v21)</sup> That thou hast slain my children, and delivered them to cause them to pass through the fire for them?
>
> <sup>[22](/bible/ezekiel/16#v22)</sup> And in all thine abominations and thy whoredoms thou hast not remembered the days of thy youth, when thou wast naked and bare, and wast polluted in thy blood.

- She took her sons and daughters, whom she had borne unto the Most High, and sacrificed them to the images to be devoured, causing His children to pass through the fire.
- In all her abominations and whoredoms she did not remember the days of her youth, when she was naked and bare and polluted in her own blood.

**[Ezekiel 16:23-26](/bible/ezekiel/16#v23)**

> <sup>[23](/bible/ezekiel/16#v23)</sup> And it came to pass after all thy wickedness, (woe, woe unto thee! saith the Lord God;)
>
> <sup>[24](/bible/ezekiel/16#v24)</sup> That thou hast also built unto thee an eminent place, and hast made thee an high place in every street.
>
> <sup>[25](/bible/ezekiel/16#v25)</sup> Thou hast built thy high place at every head of the way, and hast made thy beauty to be abhorred, and hast opened thy feet to every one that passed by, and multiplied thy whoredoms.
>
> <sup>[26](/bible/ezekiel/16#v26)</sup> Thou hast also committed fornication with the Egyptians thy neighbours, great of flesh; and hast increased thy whoredoms, to provoke me to anger.

- After all her wickedness the Most High cries woe, woe unto her; she built herself an eminent place and made a high place in every street, at the head of every way.
- Those high places in every street are the churches of today; here in America we see the coexist mindset, accepting every religion, while the Most High gave us the commandments, and now those religions have become a stronghold unto us.
- She committed fornication with the Egyptians, her great-fleshed neighbors, the same people that enslaved us four hundred years, much like we do today, provoking the Most High to anger.

**[Ezekiel 16:27-29](/bible/ezekiel/16#v27)**

> <sup>[27](/bible/ezekiel/16#v27)</sup> Behold, therefore I have stretched out my hand over thee, and have diminished thine ordinary food, and delivered thee unto the will of them that hate thee, the daughters of the Philistines, which are ashamed of thy lewd way.
>
> <sup>[28](/bible/ezekiel/16#v28)</sup> Thou hast played the whore also with the Assyrians, because thou wast unsatiable; yea, thou hast played the harlot with them, and yet couldest not be satisfied.
>
> <sup>[29](/bible/ezekiel/16#v29)</sup> Thou hast moreover multiplied thy fornication in the land of Canaan unto Chaldea; and yet thou wast not satisfied herewith.

- Therefore the Most High stretched out His hand, diminished her ordinary food, and delivered her to the will of them that hate her, the daughters of the Philistines, which are ashamed of her lewd way.
- She played the whore with the Assyrians and yet could not be satisfied, and multiplied her fornication in the land of Canaan unto Chaldea, and still was not satisfied.

**[Ezekiel 16:30-34](/bible/ezekiel/16#v30)**

> <sup>[30](/bible/ezekiel/16#v30)</sup> How weak is thine heart, saith the Lord God, seeing thou doest all these things, the work of an imperious whorish woman;
>
> <sup>[31](/bible/ezekiel/16#v31)</sup> In that thou buildest thine eminent place in the head of every way, and makest thine high place in every street; and hast not been as an harlot, in that thou scornest hire;
>
> <sup>[32](/bible/ezekiel/16#v32)</sup> But as a wife that committeth adultery, which taketh strangers instead of her husband!
>
> <sup>[33](/bible/ezekiel/16#v33)</sup> They give gifts to all whores: but thou givest thy gifts to all thy lovers, and hirest them, that they may come unto thee on every side for thy whoredom.
>
> <sup>[34](/bible/ezekiel/16#v34)</sup> And the contrary is in thee from other women in thy whoredoms, whereas none followeth thee to commit whoredoms: and in that thou givest a reward, and no reward is given unto thee, therefore thou art contrary.

- The Most High asks how weak her heart is, seeing she does all these things as the work of an imperious whorish woman; He gave us everything and we were not satisfied, chasing the philosophies, doctrines, and religions of the nations.
- She is not even as a harlot who scorns hire, but as a wife that commits adultery, taking strangers instead of her husband, giving gifts to all her lovers and hiring them to come unto her.
  - **[2 Corinthians 11:2](/bible/2-corinthians/11#v2)**
    > <sup>[2](/bible/2-corinthians/11#v2)</sup> For I am jealous over you with godly jealousy: for I have espoused you to one husband, that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ.

    Paul espoused us to one husband, that he may present us as a chaste virgin to Christ, so we must come out of the other religions and be committed to the law, statutes, and commandments.
  - **[Jeremiah 2:11](/bible/jeremiah/2#v11)**
    > <sup>[11](/bible/jeremiah/2#v11)</sup> Hath a nation changed their gods, which are yet no gods? but my people have changed their glory for that which doth not profit.

    A nation does not change their gods, which are yet no gods, but our people changed their glory for that which does not profit, showing everything we did never profited us.

**[Ezekiel 16:35-39](/bible/ezekiel/16#v35)**

> <sup>[35](/bible/ezekiel/16#v35)</sup> Wherefore, O harlot, hear the word of the Lord:
>
> <sup>[36](/bible/ezekiel/16#v36)</sup> Thus saith the Lord God; Because thy filthiness was poured out, and thy nakedness discovered through thy whoredoms with thy lovers, and with all the idols of thy abominations, and by the blood of thy children, which thou didst give unto them;
>
> <sup>[37](/bible/ezekiel/16#v37)</sup> Behold, therefore I will gather all thy lovers, with whom thou hast taken pleasure, and all them that thou hast loved, with all them that thou hast hated; I will even gather them round about against thee, and will discover thy nakedness unto them, that they may see all thy nakedness.
>
> <sup>[38](/bible/ezekiel/16#v38)</sup> And I will judge thee, as women that break wedlock and shed blood are judged; and I will give thee blood in fury and jealousy.
>
> <sup>[39](/bible/ezekiel/16#v39)</sup> And I will also give thee into their hand, and they shall throw down thine eminent place, and shall break down thy high places: they shall strip thee also of thy clothes, and shall take thy fair jewels, and leave thee naked and bare.

- Wherefore, O harlot, hear the word of the Most High: because her filthiness was poured out through her whoredoms with her lovers and idols, and by the blood of her children, He will gather all her lovers, both loved and hated, against her and discover her nakedness unto them.
- He will judge her as a woman that breaks wedlock and sheds blood, give her blood in fury and jealousy, deliver her into their hand to throw down her eminent place, strip her of her clothes, take her fair jewels, and leave her naked and bare.
- This is spiritual and physical: we do not control the distribution of our music, so the most vile music is put out for us and our children, showing us naked and in compromising positions, and that is what has been glorified here in America.

**[Ezekiel 16:40-43](/bible/ezekiel/16#v40)**

> <sup>[40](/bible/ezekiel/16#v40)</sup> They shall also bring up a company against thee, and they shall stone thee with stones, and thrust thee through with their swords.
>
> <sup>[41](/bible/ezekiel/16#v41)</sup> And they shall burn thine houses with fire, and execute judgments upon thee in the sight of many women: and I will cause thee to cease from playing the harlot, and thou also shalt give no hire any more.
>
> <sup>[42](/bible/ezekiel/16#v42)</sup> So will I make my fury toward thee to rest, and my jealousy shall depart from thee, and I will be quiet, and will be no more angry.
>
> <sup>[43](/bible/ezekiel/16#v43)</sup> Because thou hast not remembered the days of thy youth, but hast fretted me in all these things; behold, therefore I also will recompense thy way upon thine head, saith the Lord God: and thou shalt not commit this lewdness above all thine abominations.

- They shall bring a company against her, stone her, thrust her through with swords, and burn her houses, executing judgments in the sight of many women.
- The Most High will cause her to cease from playing the harlot and give no more hire, and then His fury and jealousy shall rest and He will be no more angry.
- Because she did not remember the days of her youth but fretted Him in all these things, He recompenses her way upon her own head.

**[Ezekiel 16:44-52](/bible/ezekiel/16#v44)**

> <sup>[44](/bible/ezekiel/16#v44)</sup> Behold, every one that useth proverbs shall use this proverb against thee, saying, As is the mother, so is her daughter.
>
> <sup>[45](/bible/ezekiel/16#v45)</sup> Thou art thy mother’s daughter, that lotheth her husband and her children; and thou art the sister of thy sisters, which lothed their husbands and their children: your mother was an Hittite, and your father an Amorite.
>
> <sup>[46](/bible/ezekiel/16#v46)</sup> And thine elder sister is Samaria, she and her daughters that dwell at thy left hand: and thy younger sister, that dwelleth at thy right hand, is Sodom and her daughters.
>
> <sup>[47](/bible/ezekiel/16#v47)</sup> Yet hast thou not walked after their ways, nor done after their abominations: but, as if that were a very little thing, thou wast corrupted more than they in all thy ways.
>
> <sup>[48](/bible/ezekiel/16#v48)</sup> As I live, saith the Lord God, Sodom thy sister hath not done, she nor her daughters, as thou hast done, thou and thy daughters.
>
> <sup>[49](/bible/ezekiel/16#v49)</sup> Behold, this was the iniquity of thy sister Sodom, pride, fulness of bread, and abundance of idleness was in her and in her daughters, neither did she strengthen the hand of the poor and needy.
>
> <sup>[50](/bible/ezekiel/16#v50)</sup> And they were haughty, and committed abomination before me: therefore I took them away as I saw good.
>
> <sup>[51](/bible/ezekiel/16#v51)</sup> Neither hath Samaria committed half of thy sins; but thou hast multiplied thine abominations more than they, and hast justified thy sisters in all thine abominations which thou hast done.
>
> <sup>[52](/bible/ezekiel/16#v52)</sup> Thou also, which hast judged thy sisters, bear thine own shame for thy sins that thou hast committed more abominable than they: they are more righteous than thou: yea, be thou confounded also, and bear thy shame, in that thou hast justified thy sisters.

- Everyone that uses proverbs shall use this proverb against her: As is the mother, so is her daughter; she is her mother's daughter that loathes her husband and children, and loathe means hate.
- Her mother was a Hittite and her father an Amorite; her elder sister is Samaria and her younger sister is Sodom, yet she was corrupt more than they in all her ways.
- The iniquity of Sodom was pride, fulness of bread, and abundance of idleness, and she did not strengthen the hand of the poor and needy; yet Samaria did not commit half of Jerusalem's sins, for Jerusalem multiplied her abominations more than them and justified her sisters, who are more righteous than she.

**[Ezekiel 16:53-59](/bible/ezekiel/16#v53)**

> <sup>[53](/bible/ezekiel/16#v53)</sup> When I shall bring again their captivity, the captivity of Sodom and her daughters, and the captivity of Samaria and her daughters, then will I bring again the captivity of thy captives in the midst of them:
>
> <sup>[54](/bible/ezekiel/16#v54)</sup> That thou mayest bear thine own shame, and mayest be confounded in all that thou hast done, in that thou art a comfort unto them.
>
> <sup>[55](/bible/ezekiel/16#v55)</sup> When thy sisters, Sodom and her daughters, shall return to their former estate, and Samaria and her daughters shall return to their former estate, then thou and thy daughters shall return to your former estate.
>
> <sup>[56](/bible/ezekiel/16#v56)</sup> For thy sister Sodom was not mentioned by thy mouth in the day of thy pride,
>
> <sup>[57](/bible/ezekiel/16#v57)</sup> Before thy wickedness was discovered, as at the time of thy reproach of the daughters of Syria, and all that are round about her, the daughters of the Philistines, which despise thee round about.
>
> <sup>[58](/bible/ezekiel/16#v58)</sup> Thou hast borne thy lewdness and thine abominations, saith the Lord.
>
> <sup>[59](/bible/ezekiel/16#v59)</sup> For thus saith the Lord God; I will even deal with thee as thou hast done, which hast despised the oath in breaking the covenant.

- When the Most High brings again the captivity of Sodom and her daughters, and of Samaria and her daughters, then He will bring again the captivity of Jerusalem in the midst of them, that she may bear her own shame.
- In the day of her pride Sodom was not so much as mentioned by her mouth, but now she bears her lewdness and abomination, having despised the oath in breaking the covenant.

**[Ezekiel 16:60-63](/bible/ezekiel/16#v60)**

> <sup>[60](/bible/ezekiel/16#v60)</sup> Nevertheless I will remember my covenant with thee in the days of thy youth, and I will establish unto thee an everlasting covenant.
>
> <sup>[61](/bible/ezekiel/16#v61)</sup> Then thou shalt remember thy ways, and be ashamed, when thou shalt receive thy sisters, thine elder and thy younger: and I will give them unto thee for daughters, but not by thy covenant.
>
> <sup>[62](/bible/ezekiel/16#v62)</sup> And I will establish my covenant with thee; and thou shalt know that I am the Lord:
>
> <sup>[63](/bible/ezekiel/16#v63)</sup> That thou mayest remember, and be confounded, and never open thy mouth any more because of thy shame, when I am pacified toward thee for all that thou hast done, saith the Lord God.

- Nevertheless the Most High will remember His covenant with her in the days of her youth and establish unto her an everlasting covenant.
- This is why the new covenant, the covenant of [Hebrews 10](/bible/hebrews/10) and [Jeremiah 31](/bible/jeremiah/31), is made only with His people; the notion that our oppressors, who glorified our fall, get the same reward is absolute foolishness and makes no biblical sense.
- When He is pacified, she shall remember her ways, be ashamed, and never open her mouth anymore because of her shame, and she shall know that He is the Lord.
  - **[Lamentations 3:22](/bible/lamentations/3#v22)**
    > <sup>[22](/bible/lamentations/3#v22)</sup> It is of the Lord’s mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not.

    It is of the Most High's mercies that we are not consumed, because His compassions fail not, and that is the compassion we are reading about here.
  - **[Zechariah 12:9-14](/bible/zechariah/12#v9)**
    > <sup>[9](/bible/zechariah/12#v9)</sup> And it shall come to pass in that day, that I will seek to destroy all the nations that come against Jerusalem.
    >
    > <sup>[10](/bible/zechariah/12#v10)</sup> And I will pour upon the house of David, and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the spirit of grace and of supplications: and they shall look upon me whom they have pierced, and they shall mourn for him, as one mourneth for his only son, and shall be in bitterness for him, as one that is in bitterness for his firstborn.
    >
    > <sup>[11](/bible/zechariah/12#v11)</sup> In that day shall there be a great mourning in Jerusalem, as the mourning of Hadadrimmon in the valley of Megiddon.
    >
    > <sup>[12](/bible/zechariah/12#v12)</sup> And the land shall mourn, every family apart; the family of the house of David apart, and their wives apart; the family of the house of Nathan apart, and their wives apart;
    >
    > <sup>[13](/bible/zechariah/12#v13)</sup> The family of the house of Levi apart, and their wives apart; the family of Shimei apart, and their wives apart;
    >
    > <sup>[14](/bible/zechariah/12#v14)</sup> All the families that remain, every family apart, and their wives apart.

    In that day He pours the spirit of grace upon the house of David, and every family mourns apart, which is the shame that comes upon us when the remembrance of our wickedness returns.
